tested_scope: Read-only schema evaluation of the currently Chat-exposed GitHub create_issue, search_issues, and fetch_issue surfaces. No GitHub issue, comment, label, branch, file, PR, release, or other external resource mutation was executed for the candidate test.
observations: create_issue exposes repository_full_name, title, body, assignees, labels, and milestone but no caller-controlled server-enforced unique/idempotency key or client issue identifier.
A token embedded in title or body is payload data, not an exposed uniqueness or idempotency contract.
search_issues exposes query/filter search rather than deterministic exact lookup by a server-enforced caller-chosen operation identity.
fetch_issue requires the server-assigned issue_number, which is exactly the value that may be unavailable when the create response is lost.
counterexample: If an issue create commits but its response is lost, the caller has no exposed pre-write server-enforced identity by which to prove that exact create committed before deciding whether a retry is safe. Reusing the same title/body token is not an idempotency contract, and the exact issue_number is unknown until a successful response. Therefore the exposed surfaces do not provide deterministic ambiguous-write reconciliation for a generic operation record.
